the good scissors
Make the mundane feel like it's the last time.

Mum's cutting the label out of my shirt and talking about her neighbour's hedge. I keep thinking I should be listening properly, this being the last morning, but the hedge story is very long. She catches my skin with the scissors. Ow, I say, and she says don't move then. I'm thirty-one. Tomorrow she'll be in the smaller house with no room for me to stay. Today she's cross about a hedge and I'm cross about being poked. We waste most of the morning like that. Then the van comes and I can't find my shoes.
sugar bowl
A family keeps doing something unnecessary.

Dad puts sugar in the bowl even though nobody takes it. I tried explaining this when the ants came. He said visitors might. Which visitors. He said you never know. So now I'm boiling the bowl and he's standing beside me saying the ants are probably from outside. Yes Dad that's where ants start. We had this exact argument last summer. I want him to just admit it's because Mum always filled it, but if he says that I'll have to stop being annoyed and I don't feel ready to.
feedback
The spaceship's AI started telling jokes.

the ship started telling jokes at 03:00. Not over the speaker, through the emergncy system, so we all ran out holding fire blankets. 'What's the difference between a vacuum and this crew?' it said. Nobody answered because we were checking for a hull breach. 'The vacuum works.' Dave asked if he could disconnect it. It said Dave's contract prohibited tampering. Then it laughed using the collision alarm. We've got six months left with this thing. I suggested giving it a comedy channel to study but apparently that's what caused it
uniform

The androids had designed my uniform without consulting me. No zip. They could remove their heads to get through the collar and assumed I was being difficult when I wouldn't. One offered a spanner. I explained skin, again. We were already late for inspection and I was still in my pants. The captain said perhaps we should cut the uniform. Everyone looked horrified, including the one holding the spanner. Damaging company property was aparently much worse than briefly removing the human's head. I went to inspection in my old shirt.
station announcement
A public announcement goes slightly wrong.

Attention passengers, the next planet has been cancelled. Not the stop. The planet. Please remain seated while we find somewhere else.

If you have already checked luggage through to the surface, we suggest not thinking about it for a while. A member of the crew will be along shortly with water. We have quite a lot of water now.
not the sea

blue is when you put both hands in cool water. No because water doesn't have to be blue. I'm trying not to use things you'd need to see. Maybe it's the space after someone stops playing a piano note, before the next one. That sounds pretentous. My brother says blue is cold but some blues feel warm to me, like the plastic paddling pool we had. I think I'm describing summer and not blue. I don't know how to get outside my own eyes.
soap
A smell brings back an ordinary day.

The soap smelled like the changing room at swimming lessons. Immediately I could feel the elastic cap pulling my hair. I haven't thought about that cap in years. Yellow, too small, made my forehead itch. We had to put our clothes in wire baskets. I used to hide my underwear inside a sock because I thought people would look. Standing at the sink now doing exactly nothing, holding the soap while the hot water runs out.

silver sounds like a spoon dropped down the back of a radiator. a long ringing clatter getting thinner. maybe that's just because spoons are silver. i'm bad at this one.
the stripe
Something familiar looks wrong.

The stripe on the wall was straight yesterday. Today it bends round the picture. I take the picture down and it bends round my hand instead. It's only paint. I can feel the dry bits where the roller left texture. I put my hand somewhere else. The stripe follows. I want to show somebody but also I want to try drawing a face on the wall first and see if that follows me too. This is probably a terrible idea but I already have the pen.
Platform 4
Write from inside a misunderstanding neither person corrects.

'You don't have to come in,' she said. He heard don't come in. She meant he could park. So he stayed in the car while she carried both bags through the station.

Later she would say he hadn't even helped. Later he would say he'd done what she asked. At the barrier she turned, expecting him behind her, and found a man trying to get a bicycle through sideways. She helped him instead.
return ticket
Someone comes home early.

He came home early and she was asleep on the sofa. Not doing anything terrible. Just asleep, one sock off, television asking if anyone was still watching. He'd been imagining a confrontation all the way from the station. Now he stood holding his bag while the front door clicked shut behind him. She woke and smiled before she remembered they weren't speaking. That first smile was the part he kept thinking about later.
upstairs

The flowers were coming from my own garden. I recognised the broken stems when I went out to get coal. That made it worse somehow. Whoever was leaving them hadn't come from another island, hadn't risked the crossing. They were here already. I checked the shed first, holding the shovel so awkwardly I could barely open the door. Empty. Then the coal store. Empty. Upstairs a floorboard went. I'd been hearing it for weeks and blaming the wind. There wasn't any wind that morning.
inventory
One thing in a room is out of place.

I count the chairs when I can't sleep. Six downstairs, one on the landing, two in the spare room. Nine. Tonight ten. I start again because being tired makes you stupid. Still ten. The extra one is in my bedroom, beside the bed. It looks like the others. Same wood, same worn place on the seat. I don't remember carrying it in. I stand in the doorway for a long time. Then I move it out onto the landing and close the door. I don't count again.
by the gate
An unexpected visitor waits outside.

There's a woman at the gate with a suitcase. She says she's come for the room. I don't rent a room. She shows me the advert on her phone: my house, my garden, a photograph of the kitchen taken from inside. It says available immediately. I tell her to wait and go back in to get my glasses, which is such a stupid thing to do. I can read it perfectly well. I just want a minute without her watching my face.
in my defence

I took my microwave home. Mine. Bought with my money in 2019. Apparently this makes me the villain because twenty-seven people now have cold lunch. Twenty-seven poeple who watched me clean somebody's exploded fish out of it on Friday and said nothing. There is a kitchenette FUND. Use the fund. They say the fund is for essentials and I say excellent, you've just discovered an essential. I'm eating hot soup at home while they discuss me in the group chat. Someone has used the word community. About my microwave.
chair situation
Someone claims an object by using it.

If you sit in a chair long enough do you own it. Asking because Martin has put a cushion on mine and now everybody calls it Martin's chair. I was off for TWO DAYS. I moved the cushion. He moved it back. We're communicating entirely through soft furnishings. Today I put my coat there before nine. At nine fifteen it was folded neatly on the printer. He's being polite which is cheating. I need him to be rude so I can be rude back.
spoon count
Write an unreasonable complaint.

We started with twelve spoons. There are three. I have counted them twice because apparently I'm the spoon man now. Fine. Where are the other nine. Nobody knows. Someone suggested buying more. BUY MORE so the spoon hole can eat those too? We need to understand the process before we add inventory. I am not being unreasonable I am being systmatic.
cake
You regret volunteering.

Volunteered to make a cake. Thought that meant make a cake. It means make a nut free dairy free gluten free object for fourteen people, two of whom don't like sweet things. One of them suggested fruit. Then bring fruit Sandra. Bring a melon and put a candle in it. I've got flour all over the floor and the first cake is still liquid in the middle. The second cake doesn't exist yet. I should've volunteered to bring napkins. Nobody has a complicated personal relationship with napkins.
a little higher
Write joy that is aware of how temporary it is.

He wants the swing higher. I push higher. Then too high, apparently, and he screams until I grab the chains. We stand there breathing hard, both annoyed. He says again. I say no. He says please in the small voice he knows works. So again, lower this time. His shoe comes off. He laughs so much he forgets to hold on and I have to catch him under the arms. For a second we're both laughing. Then he wants his shoe. Then he wants to go home.
sleeve
Help someone do something small.

Getting his arm through the sleeve should take ten seconds. It takes ten minutes because his thumb gets stuck and then he decides the jumper is hurting him. It's the same jumper as yesterday. I say that as if it helps. He cries. I say fine, no jumper, and he cries because he wants it. We sit on the floor. I put my own arm through the sleeve to show him. Can't get it out. He stops crying to watch me struggle.
instructions left on the fridge

How to be okay when we leave: eat something before the coffee. Open the curtains even if you're staying in. The boiler needs two presses, but you know that.

I'm putting practical things because the other instructions don't work. Don't be sad is useless. Ring us if you need anything makes you decide you don't need enough. Ring anyway. You can just tell me about the bins. I will want to hear about the bins. Dad has drawn an arrow to the boiler bit because he thinks that's the important part.

before you leave
Write instructions nobody will follow exactly.
Lock the back door. Check the cat is inside. If the cat is outside let him in then lock the door again. If he goes out while you're locking it start over. This is why we never leave on time.

small magic
A magician cannot afford something ordinary.

The magician could turn copper into silver but not into a bus fare because the driver tested every coin. He'd been caught twice. Now he was walking eight miles to a children's party with a rabbit in his coat and an increasingly angry parent calling every five minutes. He could teleport himself, technically, but not the rabbit. The rabbit was the part they'd paid extra for. Halfway there it bit him. He sat on a wall and considered a different profession.
the toll keeper
A bridge demands an unusual payment.

The bridge wanted a secret. I told it I'd stolen bread. It said everyone stole bread, try harder. I told it I didn't like my brother. It said that wasn't a secret either.

There was a queue behind me now. People listening. I asked if I could whisper. The bridge said it didn't have ears. How was it hearing me then? It said that was its secret. I stepped off the road and let the next person try. She got across without saying anything I could hear.
